sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Design patterns interview questions test whether you can apply the Gang-of-Four classics to real Java code — Singleton (and why it is a smell), Factory and Abstract Factory, Builder (with the Java records angle), Strategy, Observer, Decorator, Adapter, Proxy, and the patterns Spring itself uses (Template Method, IoC, AOP). Each answer leads with the problem the pattern solves, the Java implementation, and the trade-offs (when not to use it).

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Three families — name the family before the pattern.

- **Creational** — Factory, Abstract Factory, Builder, Singleton, Prototype.
- **Structural** — Adapter, Decorator, Facade, Proxy, Composite, Bridge, Flyweight.
- **Behavioural** — Strategy, Observer, Template Method, Command, State, Iterator, Chain of Responsibility.

**Spring uses many** by default — DI ≈ inversion-of-control, AOP ≈ proxy, `JdbcTemplate` ≈ template method.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Behavioral patterns** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Comparisons** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Creational patterns** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Design patterns legacy** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Refactoring** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Solid principles** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Structural patterns** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Technical debt** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Scenario-based** — applied questions tying multiple topics together. Drill these *last*, after the fundamentals are sharp.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Singleton is a smell** when global state lurks — prefer DI scope.
- **Strategy vs State** — same shape, different intent: strategy is interchangeable, state is contextual.
- **Builder for records** — modern Java needs less of it.
- **Composition is the meta-pattern** — most patterns are composition in disguise.
- **Anti-patterns count too** — God object, anaemic domain, magic numbers.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"This problem is a classic <pattern> from the <creational | structural | behavioural> family — it gives me <intent>. The trade-off is <indirection cost>, and I'd skip the pattern when <simpler-shape suffices>."*
